definition: A 32B Qwen trained with a group-relative variant, and across 3 sources the archive's reference reinforcement-learning-trained model in the reasoning-boundary debate. It is the model on which chain-scored pass@k reverses the plain-pass@k verdict, showing a consistent and significant gap in its favour against its base at every budget up to 1024. It is also where symbolic variabilisation shows scaling raising raw accuracy without fixing consistency -- 92.3 to 69.8 percent on one set under the strict metric, with the loose partial-credit metric narrowing that to 7.2 percent, which separates memorisation from inconsistency. And it is one of the four model families in the branch-preference measurement showing entropy collapse concentrated in semantic rather than syntactic contrasts.

evidence.note: Builds prefix trees of semantically equivalent reasoning statements and measures how RLVR changes a model's preference between branches, finding the entropy collapse is not stylistic — the collapse is stronger for semantically distinct continuations than for syntactic variants of the same statement.
evidence.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

evidence.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
evidence.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: DAPO-Qwen-32B
